summary: Lake County, MN steel stairway tower on Superior National Forest land; county list says removed, the 1988 USFS record says dismantled in the 1960s with foundations remaining.

facts.design: Steel stairway tower (county list); 100-foot tower with log cabin and garage (1988 USFS record)
facts.status_note: Tower removed; foundations remain per the 1988 USFS record
facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service (county list); the 1988 USFS record credits the Civilian Conservation Corps with building it

staffing.status: watched for fires by the nearby Spruce Lake CCC camp (county list)

access.note: On National Forest land; the Forest Service directions end at a dead-end forest road near the old lookout site. No closure or permit requirement found in the sources read.

visit.trail_note: Directions end at a dead end of FR-836 near the old lookout site (1988 USFS record); no tower remains to climb

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1952 county survey note gives 110 feet and the county list says probably 100 feet; the 1988 USFS record describes a 100-foot tower. The record uses 100 feet and the story reports the 110-foot note.
The county list calls it a USFS stairway tower; the 1988 USFS record says the CCC built it on land the state kept for a lookout. Both are recorded and reported.

notes_for_editor: Best documented of the three. The 1988 USFS establishment record is read from a DocsLib copy with OCR errors (the 1960s and 1930s dates are garbled, so the clean quotes come from kjackson.us, which repeats the same passage). Builder and height conflict between the county list and the USFS record. Access level 'public' is our reading (National Forest land, directions to a dead-end road near the site, no closure stated), not a stated opening. Events for 1930 and 1960 are decade-only dates; the year shown is the decade start and the note says so. No image URLs were read, so no photos added. Two searches used.
